s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lateral knee pain with an intra-articular space-occupying lesion
salient_findings: Recurrent pain localized to the lateral side of the left knee
Intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau on MRI
Lesion with heterogeneous appearance and peripheral rim enhancement on MRI
key_facts: 30-year-old Asian man
6-month history of recurrent pain
Pain localized to the lateral side of the left knee
Slight tenderness and swelling over the lateral joint line
Plain radiographs were unremarkable
Routine laboratory tests were within normal limits
MRI demonstrated a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion
Lesion invaded the tibial plateau
Lesion was homogeneous and isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images
Lesion appeared heterogeneous with internal specks on T2-weighted images
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed enhancement confined to the peripheral rim of the mass

differentials: Clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue
Intraosseous pleomorphic hyalizing angiectatic tumor of bone
Intra-articular desmoplastic small round cell tumor
per_call: Clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue
Intraosseous pleomorphic hyalizing angiectatic tumor of bone
Intra-articular desmoplastic small round cell tumor

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of intra-articular space-occupying lesions in the knee

shortlist.label: Chondroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents with pain and swelling, and can have a similar appearance on MRI

shortlist.label: Synovial chondromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by multiple intra-articular cartilaginous nodules, which can cause pain and swelling

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause recurrent pain and swelling, and has a distinctive appearance on MRI

shortlist.label: Chondromyxoid fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can present with pain and swelling, and has a characteristic appearance on MRI

raw.rationale: The lesion's location in the epiphysis or apophysis, particularly invading the tibial plateau, and its appearance on MRI with a heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images and peripheral rim enhancement, are consistent with chondroblastoma, a rare, benign tumor that typically affects the epiphyses of long bones in young adults.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
rejected.why: Typically occurs in skeletally mature individuals and has a more aggressive appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Synovial chondromatosis
rejected.why: Characterized by multiple intra-articular cartilaginous nodules, which were not described in this case

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: Typically shows diffuse synovial involvement and hemosiderin deposition, not seen in this case

rejected.label: Chondromyxoid fibroma
rejected.why: Rarely invades the tibial plateau and typically has a more homogeneous appearance on MRI
